text:
Jamal: CI SCA just flagged a transitive lib used by the runtime image: fastjson-lite -> CVE-2026-0452. Failing the release gate. Need quick risk decision, we’re in the final cutoff window.
Priya: Can you paste the vuln details? severity/attack vector?
Jamal: From Snyk: "CVE-2026-0452: Improper input validation in fastjson-lite <=1.2.4 allows deserialization leading to arbitrary object injection (high)". Affects our image builder pipeline only at image-parse-time, not plaintext parsing in API path. Repro steps attached by scanner.
OpsBot: [automated] snyk test completed on repo redwood/runtime-builder @ 1768123400. Vulnerabilities found: 1 high, 2 medium.
Lucy: Is fastjson-lite pulled into runtime via openlite-serializer@0.9.0? IIRC we vendor that in the builder image.
Jamal: Yes — transitive via openlite-serializer. openlite-serializer pinned to 0.9.0 in Dockerfile. vendor/ contains fastjson-lite-1.2.3.jar
Marco: Release schedule note: patch cutoff in ~36 hours. If this is blocking, we need either an emergency patch or a temporary mitigation plan that security signs off on.
Priya: Quick risk triage: exploitation requires the builder process to deserialize untrusted inputs. Our builder runs in CI with checked-out code from PRs and from our private git. Two threat models: (1) malicious third-party package in upstream registry (supply chain), (2) attacker controlling repo content in a PR. For (1) lower probability; for (2) higher if a CI pipeline runs untrusted PRs without sandboxing.
Lucy: Our PR builders run in ephemeral runners with limited network egress and no KMS access. But image build sometimes uses a helper that decompresses upstream artifacts — that is the vulnerable path.
Jamal: Proposed temporary mitigations: (A) Block builds that fetch external artifacts during cutoff window (config flag), (B) Add in-pipeline sanitization check: run `jar -tf vendor/fastjson-lite-1.2.3.jar` signature verification against internal allowlist, (C) Enforce manual review for any PR that touches vendor/ or Dockerfile, (D) Add audit logging for any build that uses fastjson-lite runtime (log KMS usage and env vars redacted).
Priya: Also recommend rotating any short-lived keys used by builder agent (KMS note) and ensuring builder agent does not have write access to registries. That's a compensating control.
SecurityBot: [policy] temp-risk-ack required: include owner, compensating controls, expiration date, and rollback plan.
Marco: Owner: Lucy (build infra). Proposed expiration: 7 days. Rollback if exploit observed: immediate halt of builds and emergency CVE response playbook.
Lucy: I can enforce the config flag and manual review setting by EOD. For the signature check I’ll add a lightweight script: ```bash
# verify vendor jar against internal checksum list
sha256sum vendor/fastjson-lite-1.2.3.jar | grep -Ff infra/allowed-checksums.txt
``` That will be added to the pre-build step.
Jamal: Sounds good. For audit logs, can we emit an event to AuditStream with fields: repo, commit, builder-run-id, artifact-list, and a boolean `uses_fastjson_lite`? We should also annotate with KMS key id used during build.
Priya: Yes — add `builder_run.metadata.uses_fastjson = true` and route to low-latency logging (1y retention for now) so SOC can query quickly. Also create a SOC watch for any unexpected egress from builder containers.
Marco: Timeline: Lucy implements build blocker + script by EOD today. Priya will create SOC watch and rotate ephemeral keys tomorrow morning. Jamal will update release notes to mark the allowed exception with expiration 7 days.
Jamal: For the formal temp acceptance request, required fields per policy: vulnerability id + link, scope of impact, compensating controls, owner, expiration timestamp, and evidence that build uses are limited. I’ll fill that out after this thread.
Priya: Quick Q: Are we comfortable with a 7-day window, or do we push for upstream patch first? Do we have an upstream maintainer reply ETA?
Lucy: I opened an issue/PR upstream at 2026-03-18 14:12 UTC. They acknowledged and said they’ll try a patch in ~3 days but no firm SLA.
Jamal: Given cutoff timeline, 7 days aligns with upstream ETA. We'll require re-evaluation at 72 hours and revoke the exception earlier if exploit indicators found.
SecurityBot: [action] Temporary acceptance recorded pending doc: /policies/temp_risk/1768123456. Expiration: 1768738256 (7 days).
Marco: Add to release checklist: if the exception is in place, checkbox "compensating controls verified" must be ticked or release blocked.
Lucy: Implemented the pre-build checksum script and the build flag: `DISABLE_EXTERNAL_FETCH=1` in buildkite. Pushed PR #2841.
OpsBot: [ci] buildkite/pr-2841 passed checks @ 1768126000.
Jamal: I submitted the formal temp-acceptance doc: short-lived-exception-1768123456.md with justification and controls. Linking here: https://redwood.internal/policy/temp_risk/1768123456
Priya: I created SOC watch and rotated builder ephemeral keys. Also filed follow-up ticket to run fuzzing on openlite-serializer to find other deserialization paths.
Marco: Ok, we’ll proceed with release under the temporary acceptance. Reminder: enforce manual review + no external fetch during the window.
Lucy: Will monitor for any builder anomalies and post updates in #infra-status.
Jamal: Thanks all. Closing thread — will update policy doc if upstream releases a patched fastjson-lite and we’ll remove the exception immediately. :white_check_mark:
